text: The Trace of Night item, obtained after defeating a Night Lord, is described as dimly revealing the contours of a greater being beyond the Night Lord.

The Recluse's Remembrance item, a bone-like stone bestowed by the Night Lord and given to the Recluse, is described as the bone of an Outer God capable of expunging divine essence while also being destructible by that same essence.
The Night Lord did not create the power of the Night himself; rather it came to him in the dead of night, embodied in the Primordial Night Lord's Rune.

The Primordial Night Lord's Rune, dropped by the final boss of Nightreign, is described as possessing the same nature as a Great Rune, suggesting it may be a great rune akin to those of the Elden Ring and could explain the Night Lord's power, though it is never explicitly called a Great Rune of the Elden Ring.

The Night of the Beast relic describes a three-headed wolf pup named Gladius, feared and driven from its pack, who seized a man's sword in its jaws but was shown kindness instead of harm, and has remained at the man's side ever since.
The Cord End is one of the rarest items in Limgrave, with a drop rate of about 0.035%, found inside boxes located in churches.

The Cord End's description states it belonged to young girls housed in a secret place, sacrificed by the Cutting-Gifted Tribe as part of a ritual that vowed to conceal the truth, though the girls were too young to willingly comply.
Sacrificial Twigs are talismans consumed instead of losing runes upon death, fashioned from a slender dried twig believed to have been pruned from the Erdtree long ago.
The upper branches of the Sacred Tree culminate in two tree-like hands, differing from the hands seen in the Spiral Tree Seal of the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC.
Inscriptions in the Round Table Hold's crypt, called the 'ways of cutting' (guidance of cutting in Japanese), describe sending cuttings or branches to distant lands.

One coffin inscription states that the 'ways of cutting' point to Windwhalenull, bestowing branches to those who wander and roam, which the theorist connects to Wylder and the Duchess's adoptive clan.
Another coffin inscription states that the 'ways of cutting' point to the deep woods, bestowing branches to those who are worthy and wise, which the theorist connects to the Recluse's people.
An inscription states that once the Night is broken, the Hold shall crumble and those bound to it shall be freed.

A torn scrap of paper written by an ancient people describes a loophole: if the Round Table Hold is remade through the creation of a new Night Lord, the priestess might be freed from her binding when that new Night Lord's power is lost.
The weapons left behind by defeated Night Lords are described as intimate objects whose item descriptions contain the richest lore about each Night Lord's nature and history.
Balancer's weapon item descriptions and surrounding environmental evidence encode a specific debt that Limveld's civilization incurred and never repaid.

The Primordial Night Lord's Rune description states that the Cutting-Gifted Tribe anticipated the coming Night and planned to cheat a god, having glimpsed 'the very sin of the erdtree,' for which they were punished.
Wilder carries a sword, shield, and an earring whose matching counterpart has been lost to time.
As a reward for the wet stone errand, Wilder receives relics including an earring belonging to the Priestess, which he borrows before returning it.
Holding the earring to light reveals a message: 'Two horses gallop side by side. May the wind spur us on our path,' indicating it is part of a matching set with the Priestess's earring.
Weather Vain's grave can be found in Limveld; retrieving her notes and returning them to Raider changes his advice to let the Duchess pursue multiple paths.
The Duchess blesses an iron coin given by Wilder, transforming it into the Blessed Coin, which can tie the Iron Menial to Wilder beyond the Round Table.
The Recluse instructs Wilder to find a Larval Tear, an item created by the Nox to produce silver tears used to create their Lord of Night.
The lore of the cursed blades is told across three tomes, two of which must be found in the lands between, including one guarded by a Guardian Golem near Limveld.
One tome reveals the cursed blades were crafted by a master of curses under contract to an army seeking victory.
The third tome reveals that the Recluse created the cursed blades using the Harmonious Brooch, originally meant to calm winds but repurposed for war.
The Revenant uses the incantation Triple Rings of Light, a Golden Order Fundamentalist spell gifted by Miquella to Radagon, suggesting a connection to nobility or the royal capital.
The Revenant also wields Death Lightning, a spell associated with Godwyn the Golden's battle against the ancient dragons.
The Revenant's weapon description notes her resonance with the spiritual realm, likely because she is not truly alive, explaining her summoning abilities.
The Golden Hippo drops a Night Shard upon its death.
The tooth marks on the Night Shard match those left by the ancient beast from the legend, suggesting a link to the Night Lord's origin.
The Recluse finds a Vestige of Night on a bed, serving as proof of the Night Lord's past presence.
The Night Shard bears teeth marks implying the infant bit it and was empowered by the essence of night.
The Duchess tasks the Executor with retrieving an Altus Bloom and a Golden Seed, items renamed from the Grace of Gold, which no longer exists due to the Night's spread.
A Golden Sprout is found growing in a snowy tundra despite the Night's dominance, symbolizing that the Erdtree's light endures even under corruption.
The sketch accompanying Chapter 5 depicts the Suncatcher Sword, implying the painter once owned it or was simply sketching the blade wielded by the Executor.
If the painter was from the Land of Reeds, this could explain her connection to the Suncatcher Sword, since no Crucible Knight in Elden Ring wields anything similar.
Maris's relic states the being was roused from an aimless existence by curiosity about the strange taste of the Night.
Libra's relic states it became obsessed with the concept of impartiality and viewed the Night as a champion of balance.

The Night Shard from the Recluse's questline states that the Night's reach is limitless and its touch indiscriminate, implying the Night existed as a concept before the infant bit it, since the shard already bore bite marks.
Defeating Fell Omen grants the Fell Omen Fetish, a withered version of Margit's Shackle used to subdue him in his boss fight.
The Fell Omen Fetish's description states its magic has faded, leaving only a dark stain, and that 'the protector of gold yet stands guard over the realm, even after being swallowed by the Night.'
